text:
maria: Sam in the trial is seeing intermittent stalled streaming responses and occasional connection resets behind their corporate proxy. POC is Thurs — can we swarm?

sam: Yep, reproduces in both our TS frontend and a small Python repro. Streaming stalls after ~30–60s, sometimes a 502 or ECONNRESET. No obvious rate-limit from our side.

jake: Can you paste the client logs? Are you using our node SDK or calling REST directly?

sam: Using @redwood/js sdk v0.9.2 in Electron (TS) and simple requests in Python for a backstop. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] request id=abc123 stream chunked: write EPIPE
[2026-03-18T15:12:33Z] upstream reset: read ECONNRESET
[2026-03-18T15:12:35Z] http status=502 from proxy.corp (proxy-auth ok)
```

olivia: Looks like the corporate proxy is aborting long-lived connections. Two levers: enable keepAlive on the client agent and reduce idle window / add application-level heartbeats, or switch to frequent small fetches (polling) instead of a single long stream.

jake: For TS node SDK try: 
```
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 16, keepAliveMsecs: 30000 })
const client = new RedwoodClient({ agent, timeout: 60000, streaming: true })
```
This keeps TCP sockets alive and avoids OS-level resets from the proxy. Also explicit timeouts stop hung promises.

kevin: Also important for corp proxies: some mutate chunked requests or close idle sockets aggressively. Try forcing connection-level keepalive at OS level (SO_KEEPALIVE) or add small progress pings in the stream.

sam: Tried the agent change — better but still saw a reset after ~45s. Proxy team says they close streams > 40s.

maria: Proxy policy is the blocker for the POC then. Any workaround we can ship quickly that doesn't need infra changes?

jake: Two quick workarounds: 1) disable streaming and consume via polling (shorter requests every 2–3s) or 2) chunk the prompt into smaller increments and stitch on client side. Both avoid a single socket > 40s.

sam: Python snippet we used for polling: 
```
# using requests
s = requests.Session()
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=10, pool_maxsize=10, max_retries=Retry(total=3, backoff_factor=0.5)))
resp = s.post(url, json=payload, timeout=30)
```

olivia: If they want streaming semantics, try short-lived SSE windows: request partial tokens every 5–10s and re-open the stream — gives near-real-time while staying under proxy thresholds.

support-bot: Incident #POC-3247 created to track proxy timeout policy + triage steps. Assigned to olivia + jake.

jake: Also watch for proxy that rewrites Transfer-Encoding. If they convert chunked -> buffered, you can hit 502 after buffer size exceeded. Ask proxy team if they rewrite or inspect bodies.

sam: Confirmed proxy does deep inspection and buffers up to ~1MB. Long LLM streams hit that.

kevin: For the immediate demo, easiest path: disable streaming in SDK for the demo, set timeout=45s, and fall back to polling. I'll prepare an updated quickstart snippet for the customer.

maria: Pricing question from procurement—if they move from streaming to polling, token cost goes up due to repeated context. Should we estimate delta?

jake: Estimate: polling every 3s with partial tokens likely ~+10–30% token usage depending on prompt shape. I'll attach a small calc after we know average tokens per poll.

sam: We switched to polling for the demo and it passed. No more 502s. Will loop in proxy team for a permanent fix (keepalive/allowlist). Thanks all.

maria: Great — I'll update the POC status and follow up on pricing + security questionnaire. Closing this thread once I have the procurement note. :thumbsup:
